newsitem.title: USA: NFL-SHULA HEADS 1997 PRO FOOTBALL HALL OF FAME CLASS.
newsitem.headline: NFL-SHULA HEADS 1997 PRO FOOTBALL HALL OF FAME CLASS.

text.p: Don Shula, who recorded more victories than any coach in NFL history and coached in a record six Super Bowls, on Saturday was elected to the Pro Football Hall of Fame in his first year of eligibility.

Joining Shula in the class of 1997 was former Patriots and Raiders defensive back Mike Haynes, former Pittsburgh Steelers centre Mike Webster and, from the contributors category, New York Giants owner Wellington Mara.
"It's fantastic. I just can't tell you how great I feel," said the 67-year-old Shula, looking trim and tanned as ever.

"When you think about the people that are in the Hall of Fame and what they have contributed to the sport that's meant so much to me and my family, it's another reason why I'm overwhelmed by what's happened," added Shula, who spent 33 years as head coach of the Baltimore Colts and Miami Dolphins.
There was never any doubt that Shula's place in the Canton, Ohio, shrine was secure.
He posted a remarkable overall record of 347-173-6, was the first coach to take two different teams to the Super Bowl and remains the only coach ever to lead an NFL team through a perfect season.
His Dolphins completed a 17-0-0 season in 1972 with a victory over the Washington Redskins in Super Bowl VII. Shula's Dolphins also won the Super Bowl the following year.
He recalled his first Super Bowl news conference in 1969 taking place in a hotel lobby lounge.
"I think it's a little bigger than that now, a few more people covering the Super Bowl than they did in those days," Shula told a room filled with reporters.
"That was Super Bowl III and that's the last thing I'm going to say about Super Bowl III," he joked of the game in which his heavily favoured Colts lost to the upstart New York Jets.
Haynes was a nine-time Pro Bowl selection in his seven seasons with the New England Patriots and seven with the Raiders.

Haynes, who was in his third year of eligibility for election to the Hall, was a starting cornerback and had an interception in Super Bowl XVIII, a 38-9 victory by the Raiders over the Redskins that marked the last time an AFC team has won the Super Bowl.
"It's a dream come true for me to be elected in the Hall of Fame," Haynes said by telephone when contacted at a Florida golf course.

Shula paid Haynes the ultimate tribute a coach can give an opposing player. Shula said that when his Dolphins played against one of Haynes's teams, he usually has his quarterbacks throw the ball to the other side of the field.
"I just think he rewrote the book on playing defensive back," Shula said of Haynes.
Webster, who played 17 seasons in the NFL, was a member of all four Super Bowl champion Pittsburgh teams and a nine-time Pro Bowl selection.
